A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rich-BLL research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched, including v1 Appendices B–D becoming v2 Appendices C–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression, contextual-bandit, classification, and OOD results in Tables 2–5, plus a subsampling ablation in Appendix D. Some bandit comparator results are explicitly borrowed, but the proposed method has original results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and additionally reports empirical NTK spectrum analyses in Appendix B, Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: The least-squares feature projection, Cholesky transformation, posterior computation, and uniform subsampling procedure are retained. The expanded backbone description does not establish an architecture change; Equation (4)'s correction concerns the probabilistic formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same five UCI datasets, Wheel Bandit difficulty levels, CIFAR-10 classification, wine/SVHN/CIFAR-100 OOD settings, and toy examples. The added spectral diagnostics concern the existing regression and classification backbones.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in each corresponding experiment in Tables 2–5. The revised Concrete scores retain the same baseline methods, and the new spectral analyses introduce no competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a diagnostic procedure examining descending empirical NTK eigenvalues and cumulative explained trace for the MLP and CNN. Existing benchmark splits, budgets, prediction metrics, and subsampling settings are retained. Naming AdamW and specifying the CNN disclose details without establishing changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Figures 3–4 add targeted analyses of whether the empirical NTK has low effective rank, supporting the projection's motivation. The existing subsample-size sensitivity analysis in Table 6 is unchanged and moves from Appendix D to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Mean-plus-standard-error reporting and the stated 20 regression seeds and 10 bandit/wine-OOD seeds are unchanged. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Concrete NLL for Dropout from 3.15±0.02 to 3.19±0.02, Ensemble from 3.19±0.03 to 3.15±0.03, and SWAG from 3.15±0.03 to 3.19±0.03. Figures 3–4 newly report concentrated NTK spectra. Rich-BLL benchmark scores and Tables 3–6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B adds an exact-recovery lemma under rank conditions, a projection-residual definition and identity, and a bound propagating training/test feature errors to posterior covariance error, with proofs. This substantially extends v1's variance-dominance and subsampling theory. Equation (4) also adds observation-noise variance, and Appendix A.1 corrects the use of full versus projected features.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same claims about scalable NTK-enriched BLL inference, conservative variance, subsampling guarantees, and empirical uncertainty quality. Adding image classification to the conclusion restates coverage already claimed and evaluated in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix B explicitly qualifies the spectral-decay motivation: low effective rank alone does not ensure alignment with the last-layer feature span. It also explains the separate roles of training/test projection residuals and increased sensitivity at low observation noise. Existing benchmark interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the previously generic CNN through its seven convolutional layers, channel widths, normalization, pooling, 0.2 dropout, and approximate parameter count. Appendices D.1–D.2 also identify AdamW where v1 said Adam-based or Adam-type optimizer. These improve implementation documentation.

R1.justification: The introduction repositions Mukhoti et al. (2023) from supporting a statement about costly beyond-last-layer Laplace methods to describing alternative deterministic uncertainty estimators. The broader related-work positioning is retained; other reference changes largely update bibliographic information or titles of matched works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and notation clarifications, adds acknowledgements and conference publication text, and inserts Appendix B with corresponding cross-reference changes. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two paired spectrum/cumulative-trace figures, expands Table 1's caption to define its symbols, and adjusts some Table 2 boldface. Existing Figures 1–2 and table structures are retained, with surrounding text and appendices reflowed.

improvement.justification: The conditional projection analysis in Appendix B, corrected noisy predictive distribution, and detailed CNN specification improve theoretical clarity and reproducibility. The gain is limited because the new spectra do not measure the training/test projection residuals required for fidelity to the full NTK; the suggestion that those residuals are small remains unverified. Benchmark evidence and central conclusions are largely unchanged.
